This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that, on 08.03.2021 at about 8.50 p.m, when the petitioner was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-43-V-7964 from International Airport CISF Junction towards Begur Signal.

At that time Indigo company tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-43-6533 having 4 trolley loaded with garbage bins was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and without any indicator or signal suddenly came to the left side of the road, as a result the petitioner lost control over his vehicle and dashed to the four trolleys loaded with garbage were connected / attached to the Tractor.
As a result of impact, petitioner fell down on the road had sustained grievous injuries on head and other parts of the body and underwent many surgeries.

It is further urged that, immediately after the accident he was shifted to Astra Hospital wherein took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Kanva Sri Sai Hospital, and then to Ambedkar Medical College, wherein he took treatment as an outpatient and underwent surgery.
It is specifically urged that he has spent more than Rs.10 lakhs towards medical and other incidental expenses.
It is specifically urged that, due to the accidental injuries he is unable to work as such he suffered both financially and emotionally.
It is further urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tractor.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the Tractor and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
This respondent has denied that the accident was caused due to the negligence of the driver of the tractor.

Percontra it is contended that while returning after dumping the garbage at the said place and time, when the tractor was being driven between CISF Signal to Begur Signal, the petitioner collided with back portion of the fourth empty trolley which was connected to the tractor.
At the time of colliding with the tractor the petitioner was riding his motorcycle without wearing helmet at a very high speed and in rash and negligent manner.
Hence is solely responsible for the occurrence of accident.
The respondent No.1 admitted that he is the RC owner of the Tractor and was duly insured with the respondent No.2 and same was in force as on the date of accident.

It is stated that the driver of the Tractor by name Sunil Kumar Yadav is employee as a driver with Agile Airport Services Pvt.Ltd., and was authorized to drive heavy motor vehicles (HMV) on the date of accident.
It is further urged that in case if court comes to conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for any compensation same is to be fastened on the 2 nd Respondent - insurance company.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. After service of notice, respondent No.2 spurred in rush to the Court by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-43-6533.

However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms &
conditions of the policy.
Non -compliance of section's 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act is pleaded.

This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and Anil Kumar M. Alias Anil Kumar vs Inter Globe Aviation (Indigo) on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8618532/

In fact the petitioner was also not wearing helmet and also not possessing valid DL at the time of alleged accident.

5. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he met with a Road Traffic Accident on 08.03.2021 at about 8.50 p.m near International Airport CISF Junction, Towards Begur Signal, Bengaluru City and sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of Tractor NH-3030 bearing Reg.No.KA-43-6533 ?
2) Whether the Petitioner proves that he is entitled to the compensation amount claimed ?
If so from whom and to what extent ?
3) What order or award ?

The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.50,00,000/- together.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, on 08.03.2021 at about 8.50 p.m, when the petitioner was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 43-V-7964 from International Airport CISF Junction towards Begur Signal.

At that time Indigo company tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-43-6533 having 4 trolley loaded with garbage bins was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and without any indicator or signal suddenly came to the left side of the road, as a result the petitioner lost control over his vehicle and dashed to the four trolleys loaded with garbage were connected / attached to the Tractor.

sentences.text: Perusal of the evidence on record i.e, spot mahazar and spot sketch marked at Ex.P3 and 4 makes it evident that the petitioner who was proceeding from Airport CISF Junction towards Begur Signal and while so proceeding in between CISF Junction, the driver of the Tractor came from same direction in rash and negligent manner, without giving any indications or signal, suddenly steered his Tractor to left side road at the same time the rider of the motorcycle / petitioner was coming from back side and dashed against the rear side of the trolleys attached to the tractor.
This collision resulted in the occurrence of the accident.

The jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of the Tractor for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 337, 338 of IPC and 134(A&B) r/w 187 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
14. No doubt the rider of the motorcycle i.e., the petitioner herein had a clear line of vision and could not have missed seeing the tractor which was taking left turn.

But the very act of the driver of the Tractor along with trolleys was drive the same in rash and negligent manner that too without putting on the indicators itself depicts that he did not exercise the degree of care which is expected of a prudent driver.
What also deserves notice is that the accident has occurred at 8.50 p.m., at which time it would be totally dark.

Under such circumstances, it appears in all probability that by the time the petitioner realized the fact that the tractor was taking turn, it would have been too late for him to react and check or divert his vehicle to avoid collision.
In this view of the matter no negligence has to be attributed on the part of the petitioner.

The driver of the tractor / trolleys who had failed to adhere to the basic rules & regulations and acted in a gross negligent manner in taking turn that too without giving any indication had contributed a higher degree of negligence in the occurrence of the resultant accident.

15. It is pertinent to note that IO has given Notice u/s 133 of IMV Act and the said notice was replied as per Ex.P.9 wherein the owner of the offending Tractor / Authorized person has admitted the involvement of the vehicle.
Therefore it is crystal clear that the offending vehicle is caused accident and in the accident the petitioner sustained injury.
In the presence of these documents it could be easily held that there is negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further the contents of Ex.P.3 & 4 and Ex.P.7 charge sheet discloses that the accident took place due to rash and negligence of the driver of the Tractor.

The respondents who have denied the cause of the accident did not make any attempt to examine the driver of the Indigo Tractor in order to show that there was no negligence on his part in causing the accident.

16. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

sentences.text: Even here in this case the driver of the Indigo Tractor is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the Tractor and he was charge sheeted.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-43-6533.
17.
On the evidence of PW.1 and Ex.P.7 charge sheet clearly reveals that the accident occurred due to rash and negligence of driver of Tractor.
Though PW.1 was cross examined at length by respondents counsel but nothing fatal was elicited so as to distrust the petitioner's version in his chief- examination.
The petitioner has satisfactorily proved that there is a negligence on the part of the driver of the Tractor in the accident.

Therefore, this Tribunal answers Issue No.1 'In the Affirmative'.
18. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the Tractor.
Therefore he is entitled for compensation.
19. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :
The petitioner has exhibited his Aadhaar card at Ex.P10.
As per Ex.P.10 Aadhar card wherein his year of birth is reflected as 1993.
This indicates that he was aged 28 years on the date of accident.

20. The petitioner deposed that prior to the accident he was doing coolie and earning Rs.30,000/-
per month.
In order to substantiate the above said fact absolutely no string of evidence is produced before this court.
When such being the case mere self serving and self proclaimed statement given by the petitioner without any string of either documentary or oral evidence cannot be trusted as to gospel truth.
It is trite law that, when the petitioner has failed to prove the income, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
The next moot question to be considered is as to how the notional income has to be considered in the eye of law.

21. It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
dated.05.07.2023.

To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on Anil Kumar M. Alias Anil Kumar vs Inter Globe Aviation (Indigo) on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8618532/

sentences.text: The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 08.03.2021.
Therefore, Rs.15,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.

22. As per the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : (i) laceration 2x1 cm over outer aspect of left eye (ii) Black eye on both sides (iii) CT Brain shows fracture of frontal bone, left orbital bone and nasal bones (iv) Left frontal subdural haematoma SAH &Left frontal lobe contusion.
It is needless to say that the injury No.l & 2 are simple and injury No.3 and 4 are grievous in nature.

The discharge summary as per Ex.P.8 of Aster CMI Hospital, Bengaluru and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Medical College indicates that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospitals for the period from 08.03.2021 to 08.03.2021 (1 days in total).
Further on perusal of discharge summary of Dr.B.R. Ambedkar Medical College and Hospital, Bengaluru indicates that he was treated from 11.03.2021 to 29.04.2021 (49 days in total).

sentences.text: On examination PW.5 found that he examined the petitioner on 09.01.2023, about 2 years and 6 months after the traumatic brain injury.
He has seen the petitioner at outpatient department on OPD basis for neurological disability assessment.
Last time the petitioner consulted the doctor on 28.07.2023.
On examination patient is conscious, obeys commands.
Patient is on wheel chair.
He cannot get up by his own, needs support of others.
His higher mental functions are impaired, his memory is also impaired.
His MMSE score is 20 (normal is 30).
At the first instance let me navigate through the evidence of PW.5 and assess the functional disability of the petitioner.

PW.5 being the Neurosurgeon he had assessed neurological disability on 24.01.2023 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has :
(i) Combined neurobehavioral and cognitive disability - 71%, (ii) Motor system disability - Minimum of 61%.
The doctor has finally opined that the petitioner has permanent whole body neurological disability of 61%.
If the cross-examination of PW.5 is perused, it becomes clear that he has not treated the petitioner.
There is no explanation for non-examination of the treated doctor.
Anyhow from a careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.5 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

Even otherwise considering the fact that the petitioner could appear before the Tribunal, lead his evidence and not only understand the questions put to him in the course of cross-examination but also give proper answers to them, the percentage of disability assessed by PW.5 is highly exaggerated.

24. Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
By applying the said precedent to the present case on hand, from the petition averments it could be culled out that petitioner is working as coolie.
Which means to say it involves lot of physical work.
The age of the petitioner also bears importance having regard to the facts of the instant case on hand.
When such is the case with a injuries sustained by the petitioner he cannot do his work effectively, as such his efficiency in work will decrease and it indirectly affect his income.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctors, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 30%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, this Tribunal consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 30%.
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the vehicle.

Therefore he is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
25.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES :
The period of hospitalization of 50 days is proved with a help of Ex.P8 discharge summaries.

During his stay in the hospital the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges as some family member of the petitioner would have accompanied him to the hospital to take him care by leaving their duties.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,200/- per day and a sum of Rs.60,000/- (1,200 X 50) is awarded under this head.

sentences.text: PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.60,000/- under this head.

27. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 4 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards Rs.60,000/- (15,000 X 4) under this head.
28. MEDICAL EXPENSES :
As per the bills marked at Ex.P14 the petitioner has spent in total Rs.4,12,256/- towards medical expenses and further he has also produced Ambulance bill at Ex.P.13 for a sum of Rs.4,000/-.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of his cross-examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitled in total for Rs.4,16,256/- which is rounded off to Rs.4,16,300/- towards medical expenses.
29. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '17'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.9,18,000/- (Rs.15,000 X 12 X 17 X 30/100) is awarded under this head.
30. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded under this head.
31. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the requirement for further treatment and the medical & incidental expenses to be incurred therefrom.
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head.

32. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Attendant charges, extra : 60,000-00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 2 Pain & sufferings : 60,000-00 3 Loss of income during laid-up : 60,000-00 period 4
Medical expenses : 4,16,300-00 5 Loss of future income due to : 9,18,000-00 disability 6 Loss of future amenities & : 40,000-00 happiness 7
Future medical expenses : - Nil - Total 15,54,300-00 33.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

sentences.text: There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-43-6533 thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
35. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms &
conditions of the policy.

opennyai_summary.issue:
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the Tractor did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
5. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, he met with a Road Traffic Accident on 08.03.2021 at about 8.50 p.m near International Airport CISF Junction, Towards Begur Signal, Bengaluru City and sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of Tractor NH-3030 bearing Reg.No.KA-43-6533 ?
2) Whether the Petitioner proves that he is entitled to the compensation amount claimed ?
If so from whom and to what extent ?

opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is specifically urged the driver of Tractor which was moving ahead of the petitioner's motorcycle with observing the traffic rules and regulations the driver had steered the tractor from right side to left side and on the same time the petitioner was coming from hind side of the trolley in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the hind side of the trolley and sustained injuries.
Further denied all the allegations made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition as against the respondents.
16. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
This collision resulted in the occurrence of the accident.
The jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of the Tractor for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 337, 338 of IPC and 134(A&B) r/w 187 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
14. No doubt the rider of the motorcycle i.e., the petitioner herein had a clear line of vision and could not have missed seeing the tractor which was taking left turn.
But the very act of the driver of the Tractor along with trolleys was drive the same in rash and negligent manner that too without putting on the indicators itself depicts that he did not exercise the degree of care which is expected of a prudent driver.
Under such circumstances, it appears in all probability that by the time the petitioner realized the fact that the tractor was taking turn, it would have been too late for him to react and check or divert his vehicle to avoid collision.
In this view of the matter no negligence has to be attributed on the part of the petitioner.
The driver of the tractor / trolleys who had failed to adhere to the basic rules & regulations and acted in a gross negligent manner in taking turn that too without giving any indication had contributed a higher degree of negligence in the occurrence of the resultant accident.
Therefore it is crystal clear that the offending vehicle is caused accident and in the accident the petitioner sustained injury.
In the presence of these documents it could be easily held that there is negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The respondents who have denied the cause of the accident did not make any attempt to examine the driver of the Indigo Tractor in order to show that there was no negligence on his part in causing the accident.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a Anil Kumar M. Alias Anil Kumar vs Inter Globe Aviation (Indigo) on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8618532/
5 particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
The petitioner has exhibited his Aadhaar card at Ex.P10.
When such being the case mere self serving and self proclaimed statement given by the petitioner without any string of either documentary or oral evidence cannot be trusted as to gospel truth.
It is trite law that, when the petitioner has failed to prove the income, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
There is no explanation for non-examination of the treated doctor.
Even otherwise considering the fact that the petitioner could appear before the Tribunal, lead his evidence and not only understand the questions put to him in the course of cross-examination but also give proper answers to them, the percentage of disability assessed by PW.5 is highly exaggerated.
24. Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
By applying the said precedent to the present case on hand, from the petition averments it could be culled out that petitioner is working as coolie.
Which means to say it involves lot of physical work.
The age of the petitioner also bears importance having regard to the facts of the instant case on hand.
When such is the case with a injuries sustained by the petitioner he cannot do his work effectively, as such his efficiency in work will decrease and it indirectly affect his income.
Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctors, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 30%, cannot be ruled out.
